Sessions.Description: District leaders are being asked to fund cybersecurity, cloud, artificial intelligence, connectivity and student safety while managing rising fixed costs and shrinking budgets. This session will demonstrate how districts can establish a clear technology-spend baseline, uncover unused services, duplicate licensing, outdated contracts and cloud or SaaS waste, and redirect recovered dollars toward priority initiatives. Sessions.Title: From Distraction to Defense: Securing K-12 Endpoints with ThreatLocker Allowlisting
Sessions.Short Title: From Distraction to Defense: Securing K-12 Endpoints with Th
Sessions.Audience: Superintendent; Assistant Superintendent; School Business Administrator; Technology Director / Manager; Curriculum & Instruction Leader; Principal / School Administrator; IT Support Staff
Sessions.Lead Title: Director of Technology and Special Projects
Sessions.Co-Presenter Details: Joseph Fulginiti (Network Engineer) @ West Deptford School District
Sessions.Description: Discover how West Deptford School District transformed its endpoint security by moving from Microsoft AppLocker and traditional EDR to ThreatLocker’s Zero Trust allowlisting platform. Beyond stopping advanced cyber threats, enforcing a Default Deny posture delivers an immediate classroom win by preventing off-task installs and games before they can ever launch. This session explores the limitations of traditional AppLocker rules at district scale and details our implementation of Ringfencing, Elevation Control, and Cyber Hero EDR. Join us to explore real-world strategies for transitioning smoothly from Learning Mode to Secured Mode without interrupting instruction, understand modern living-off-the-land attacks, and learn how a Zero Trust strategy stops adversaries from abusing trusted tools.

Sessions.Title: AI Leadership Lightning Round: Policy, Vision, Tools & Reality
Sessions.Short Title: AI Leadership Lightning Round: Policy, Vision, Tools & Reali
Sessions.Audience: Superintendent; Assistant Superintendent; School Business Administrator; Technology Director / Manager; Curriculum & Instruction Leader; Principal / School Administrator; Teacher; Board Member; Communications Staff; IT Support Staff; Library / Media Specialist

Sessions.Co-Presenters: David Aderhold; Sean Meehan; Marc Cicchino
Sessions.Co-Presenter Details: David Aderhold (Superintendent of Schools) @ West Windsor Plainsboro Regional School District; Sean Meehan (Superintendent of Schools) @ Monmouth County Vocational School District; Marc Cicchino (Director of Innovation and Special Projects) @ Northern Valley Regional High School
Sessions.Description:
AI has already been in your classrooms for years, but is your leadership strategy up to speed? In this fast-paced session, four New Jersey education leaders each take the stage for a quick, focused round, sharing some of their most valuable ideas before passing the mic to the next. You'll hear how to lead AI adoption at scale with clear policy, board support, and staff buy-in; what truly future-ready schools look like and how to start building them; the most innovative ways educators are putting today's AI tools to work; and how to turn big ideas into everyday classroom practice, from differentiated materials for multilingual learners to support for students at every skill level. Along the way, you'll get a candid look at the AI agents and assistants that are already reshaping schools and organizations around the world.

Whether you're a teacher, tech director, principal, or superintendent, you'll walk away with practical strategies and a clear plan for where to go next.

Sessions.Short Title: From Data to Action: Driving Student Success with Renaissanc

Align instructional decisions with learning goals and standards
Strengthen core instruction and intervention efforts

Whether you're evaluating assessment solutions, refining intervention practices, or seeking clearer insights across your organization, you'll leave with practical strategies for turning data into action and improving outcomes for every learner.

Sessions.Description: Have you ever struggled to find the right online resources for meaningful student enrichment? With no coding experience, he used AI-powered “vibe coding” tools to create a growing collection of engaging, school-appropriate activities tailored to students’ needs. Participants will see examples of these activities, learn how they were developed and refined, explore lessons learned along the way, and discover how educators can use AI to move from searching for resources to creating them.

Sessions.Description:
In an era where retaining talent, leveraging emerging technology, and expanding leadership capacity are critical challenges for school systems, the Sayreville School District achieved a 40% increase in non-tenured teacher retention in just one year. Through a strategic partnership with EdConnective, Sayreville implemented scalable, tech-enabled 1:1 virtual coaching to help teachers and school leaders confidently navigate pressing instructional challenges, including the rapidly evolving landscape of AI in the classroom and school community. By pairing personalized coaching with real classroom artifacts such as: video recordings, lesson plans, and strategic implementation plans, this session demonstrates how remote, data-driven coaching breaks geographic barriers to build instructional capacity, modernize teaching practices, and elevate educator satisfaction across an entire district.

Designed specifically for school and district leaders seeking replicable, operational innovations, this interactive session provides actionable guidance on AI leadership, governance, and capacity-building. District and EdConnective leaders will co-present concrete case studies and exemplars, giving attendees hands-on opportunities to evaluate real artifacts, analyze remote coaching workflows, and design sustainable support models for their own schools. Participants will leave equipped with a practical roadmap to empower educators, demystify AI integration, strengthen retention, and drive measurable student outcomes through modern professional development.

Sessions.Title: Who Unplugged the Phone?
Sessions.Short Title: Who Unplugged the Phone?
Sessions.Audience: Technology Director / Manager; IT Support Staff
Sessions.Description:
School IT teams are responsible for a huge number of systems: cameras, phones, speakers, servers, Wi-Fi devices, desktops, laptops, Chromebooks, printers, and more.

But when something goes offline, how do we find out?

Sometimes it is a ticket. Sometimes it is a phone call. And sometimes… someone tells us three days later. if not more.

In this session, I'd like to share a simple and practical approach to monitoring school technology using free self-hosted open-source tools: Uptime Kuma and NetAlertX.

I will show how these tools can be used to monitor critical systems, discover devices on the network, send alerts, and give IT teams a simple picture of what is working — and what is not.

Sessions.Title: The Lean K-12 IT Landscape: More with Less.
Sessions.Short Title: The Lean K-12 IT Landscape: More with Less.
Sessions.Audience: Superintendent; School Business Administrator; Technology Director / Manager; Decision makers
Sessions.Description:
As funding continues to decrease, grants become depleted and state and local budgets tighten, public school districts are facing another challenge, how to keep up with the ever changing educational landscape and increased costs of technology but with diminishing resources. The era of rapid-fire procurement is shifting toward a period of strategic refinement. This roundtable brings together IT leaders, innovators, network and systems administrators to discuss how to handle this. This collaborative session is designed for us tasked with balancing a modern digital learning environment against the reality of a shrinking bottom line and strategic refinement.

It’s time to shift from the flavor of the week, buzzword, shiny object phase of K-12 Educational Technologies and build a resilient, high-impact ecosystem that survives budget fluctuations and focuses on what truly matters: the student, staff and parent/guardian experience and the IT initiatives supporting it.

Let’s talk, discuss, rant, rave, plan, strategize and have a meaningful tech focused conversation about the following topics.

Strategically Audit & Axe Approach
Automation & Semi Automation & AI
Fiscal & Sustainable Responsibilities
Network & Systems Operations
Stakeholder Buy-in

Attackers don’t compromise K12 environments by targeting one security tool at a time, they exploit the gaps between your security platforms.

Sessions.Title: Students Leading the Way: Edison’s AI Journey
Sessions.Short Title: Students Leading the Way: Edison’s AI Journey
Sessions.Audience: Superintendent; Assistant Superintendent; Technology Director / Manager; Curriculum & Instruction Leader; Teacher
Sessions.Tags: AI; AI Governance; Classroom Applications; Data Analysis; Assessment & Feedback; Professional Learning
Sessions.Co-Presenter Details: Dr. Joan Valentine (Chief Academic Officer) @ Edison Twp Board of Education
Sessions.Description:
What happens when a district asks students how AI should show up in their learning? Edison Township Public Schools, one of New Jersey's largest districts, has layered its AI rollout from administrators to teacher-led AI Power Teams to students themselves, through an AI Pioneer elective, student-led teacher training, and student focus groups at its middle and high schools.

In this session, Edison shares what students have asked for (skill-building tools, clear guidance on which tools to use and when) and how the district is answering with student-facing AI activities built on its own district guidance and traffic-light protocol for appropriate use.

Attendees will also see a practical small-group workflow: using a quick Boost activity or benchmark data to group students, then generating targeted reteach, practice, and extension materials aligned to district priorities. Friction gets a bad reputation. It’s blamed for breakdowns between teachers and administrators, ruptures with parents, and the erosion of trust that follows a difficult meeting or a viral incident on social media. But friction really isn't the problem. It's poor communication. Friction exposes exactly where our systems, our relationships, and our legal frameworks are under strain, and if we really pay attention, where and how and why they need to change.
Join attorney, consultant, and law professor John Comegno as he explains how the difference between friction that damages a district and friction that improves it almost always comes down to communication: who, where, when, why, and how. Poor communication turns a disagreement into a due process filing, an AI tool into constant distraction and unnecessary action, and a struggling staff member into termination or tenure charges. The goal is to share simple, useful ideas for updating curriculum and policies so that honesty and transparency in school not only holds up, but actually grows stronger in the age of AI.

We’ll highlight the why IT needs to have a seat at the big table, professional development needs and certifications required to keep IT staff skilled and prepared, and outline the resources, planning, and support needed to sustain a resilient technology environment. Sessions.Co-Presenter Details: Kelsey Wertz (Student Success Coordinator) @ Delsea Regional School District
Sessions.Description:
When students struggle with math, traditional assessments often reveal what they got wrong, but rarely why. While sifting through various tech platforms, educators aiming to foster genuine numerical fluency must look beyond correct answers and evaluate the specific calculation strategies students use.

Grounded in the methodology of moving learners from counting to calculating, Math Diagnostic by Design equips educators to create diagnostic tasks that pinpoint exact developmental stages. Learn how to transition students off counting plateaus and onto efficient calculation pathways using visual models, spatial reasoning, and relational thinking. Join us to transform your assessment data into a clear, actionable roadmap for targeted math instruction.

This session will demonstrate how technology can provide Boards and administrators with timely data, clarify ownership and accountability, identify trends and operational concerns, and track follow-through on district priorities.
